newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RCR and Centurion to merge.
newsitem.headline: RCR and Centurion to merge.

text.p: Western Australian-based engineering companies RCR Engineering Ltd and Centurion Industries Ltd said on Friday they intended to merge.
In a joint statement, the companies said RCR would issue 11 of its shares, valued at 50 cents each for every eight Centurion shares.
This valued each Centurion share at 69 cents, equal to its net asset backing, the statement said.

Shareholders, other than Centurion's 70 percent stakeholder NatSteel Equity II Pte Ltd, would be issued a free option to take up six fully paid shares in the new company at an exercise price of 50 cents for every 10 shares held after the merger.
The merged entity would be known as RCR Centurion Engineering Ltd.
The two companies said the new body would combine the local ownership and management of RCR with the enhanced engineering assets of Centurion.
RCR shares closed on Thursday at 50 cents, for a market capitalisation of about A$9.3 million. Centurion last traded on April 23, closing at 37 cents for a market capitalisation of A$6.9 million.
NatSteel Equity II is a subsidiary of listed Singapore company NatSteel Ltd.
